question.text: Detailed analysis of sputum and systemic inflammation in asthma phenotypes: are paucigranulocytic asthmatics really non-inflammatory?
question.context: The technique of induced sputum has allowed to subdivide asthma patients into inflammatory phenotypes according to their level of granulocyte airway infiltration. There are very few studies which looked at detailed sputum and blood cell counts in a large cohort of asthmatics divided into inflammatory phenotypes. The purpose of this study was to analyze sputum cell counts, blood leukocytes and systemic inflammatory markers in these phenotypes, and investigate how those groups compared with healthy subjects. We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional study on 833 asthmatics recruited from the University Asthma Clinic of Liege and compared them with 194 healthy subjects. Asthmatics were classified into inflammatory phenotypes. The total non-squamous cell count per gram of sputum was greater in mixed granulocytic and neutrophilic phenotypes as compared to eosinophilic, paucigranulocytic asthma and healthy subjects (p < 0.005). Sputum eosinophils (in absolute values and percentages) were increased in all asthma phenotypes including paucigranulocytic asthma, compared to healthy subjects (p < 0.005). Eosinophilic asthma showed higher absolute sputum neutrophil and lymphocyte counts than healthy subjects (p < 0.005), while neutrophilic asthmatics had a particularly low number of sputum macrophages and epithelial cells. All asthma phenotypes showed an increased blood leukocyte count compared to healthy subjects (p < 0.005), with paucigranulocytic asthmatics having also increased absolute blood eosinophils compared to healthy subjects (p < 0.005). Neutrophilic asthma had raised CRP and fibrinogen while eosinophilic asthma only showed raised fibrinogen compared to healthy subjects (p < 0.005).

medgemma_4b.clinical_reasoning: The study found that paucigranulocytic asthmatics have a lower total non-squamous cell count in their sputum compared to other asthma phenotypes and healthy controls. This suggests that paucigranulocytic asthma is not truly non-inflammatory, as inflammation is present, albeit at a lower level. The increased sputum eosinophils in paucigranulocytic asthma also supports this.
medgemma_4b.critical_evidence: The study found that paucigranulocytic asthmatics have a lower total non-squamous cell count in their sputum compared to other asthma phenotypes and healthy controls.
medgemma_4b.differential_considered: The study considered other asthma phenotypes (eosinophilic, neutrophilic, mixed granulocytic/neutrophilic) and healthy controls. The findings indicate that paucigranulocytic asthma is not truly non-inflammatory, as inflammation is present, albeit at a lower level. The increased sputum eosinophils in paucigranulocytic asthma also supports this.

rnj1_8b.clinical_reasoning: The study found that paucigranulocytic asthmatics had increased sputum eosinophils and blood eosinophils compared to healthy subjects, indicating systemic inflammation. This contradicts the notion that paucigranulocytic asthmatics are non-inflammatory. The data shows eosinophilic infiltration is present in all asthma phenotypes, including paucigranulocytic asthma.
rnj1_8b.critical_evidence: Paucigranulocytic asthmatics had increased absolute blood eosinophils compared to healthy subjects (p < 0.005)
rnj1_8b.differential_considered: Considered whether paucigranulocytic asthma might represent a different disease entity, but the systemic eosinophilia and sputum eosinophil counts disprove this. The data shows eosinophilic inflammation is present in all asthma phenotypes.

qwen3_vl_8b.clinical_reasoning: The study demonstrates that even paucigranulocytic asthmatics exhibit elevated sputum eosinophils and increased blood eosinophils compared to healthy subjects, indicating systemic inflammation. The term 'paucigranulocytic' refers to low granulocyte infiltration, but does not equate to absence of inflammation. The presence of elevated eosinophils and blood leukocytes confirms ongoing inflammatory activity.
qwen3_vl_8b.critical_evidence: Paucigranulocytic asthmatics had increased absolute blood eosinophils compared to healthy subjects (p < 0.005), indicating systemic inflammation despite low sputum granulocyte counts.
qwen3_vl_8b.differential_considered: Non-inflammatory asthma was considered, but ruled out because eosinophilic infiltration and blood eosinophilia were present, confirming inflammation. Other phenotypes like neutrophilic or mixed granulocytic asthma were compared but not relevant to the question about paucigranulocytic asthma.

olmo3_7b.critical_evidence: Paucigranulocytic asthma still has increased blood eosinophil count compared to healthy subjects, indicating some inflammatory activity.
olmo3_7b.differential_considered: Other possibilities include eosinophilic or mixed phenotypes, but the key finding is that paucigranulocytic asthma does not have a dramatically increased sputum inflammatory cell count, yet it does have elevated blood eosinophils, which challenges the idea of complete absence of inflammation in this group.
